findings.text: blocking: the delivered record asserts a measurement that does not exist. manifest.md:15 states the validating measurement is "H200 job 1287671 (complete) plus job 1287676 (complete)" and manifest.md:6 states "both H200 jobs are terminal", but sacct -X -j 1287676 and squeue -j 1287676 both report 1287676 RUNNING (14 min elapsed at review time, still running), and its cited log slurm-speed-gate-fixed-1287676.log ends after the 550-cell saddle width-128 attempt, having printed only the width-1 and width-16 rows with no EXIT_550 line. The run's own exit record shows it ended at 2026-10-16T20:42:21Z against a 21:05 deadline, so the worker's turn ended while 1287676 was mid-run and no wait block was declared, leaving the 550 corrected rung unrecoverable by resume. Repair: correct manifest.md:6 and :15 to the state sacct reports and declare the job as a wait so a resume sweep can read the corrected rung when it lands.

follow-on: reference_cell_integral is dead code. Nothing in the repository calls it (grep over scripts/, tests/ and nova/ returns only its own definition), so the reuse clause it was added to satisfy is nominal: the disk split still runs through the hand-rolled integrate_disk_cell at expansion.py:102, while docs/evidence/fragments/converged-forward-solve/saddle-expansion-speed.html:42 records clause 6 as "achieved ... both imported from conic_integral.py and wrapped". The import of _quadratic at expansion.py:21 is a real reuse repair and is used on the hot path; the integrate_cell wrap is reached by nothing.

follow-on: dense_constant_elements restates the lowered-program constant enumeration the repository already owns at tests/test_equilibrium_solve.py:30 _hlo_constants (with test_compiled_chord_carries_no_state_scaled_constant at :114), which speed_gate.py could have imported the way it already imports _analytic_inputs from tests/equilibrium/test_topology_read.py. The two read different IR (StableHLO as_text versus compiler_ir("hlo")), so this is a partial rather than a full duplicate, and the done_when asked for a check "in the style of" that test; recorded for the next node rather than as a repair owed here.

follow-on: the cost decomposition is presented as two independently measured factors ("12.1 x 2.5 = 30.3 ... not a hypothesis about which term dominates"), but the product is an algebraic identity that returns the ratio by construction: (194/16) x ((6.7590/194)/(0.2230/16)) = 6.7590/0.2230 whatever the member counts are. It carries information only to the extent that 16 and 194 are the two arms' real work units, and the note asserts the control's 16 rather than showing it read from the axis arm. What survives as measurement is the ratio and the two per-member costs.
